title: Transferable Parasitic Estimation via Graph Contrastive Learning and Label Rebalancing in AMS Circuits
problem: Parasitic element estimation in AMS circuits is critical for accurate simulation but suffers from high variance and circuit-specific variation, limiting generalization across designs.
motivation: Transferable parasitic models reduce design iteration cycles and enable fast simulation-in-the-loop optimization; cross-circuit generalization is essential for large design spaces.
method: Use graph neural networks (GNN) on AMS circuit netlist representations (AIG/structural graphs) with contrastive learning objective. Apply label rebalancing to handle imbalanced parasitic distributions and improve transfer learning across circuit families.
key_novelty: Graph contrastive learning with label rebalancing for transferable parasitic element estimation across AMS circuit designs.
contributions: GNN-based parasitic extraction model with structural circuit representation
Contrastive learning objective for improved feature learning
Label rebalancing technique for skewed parasitic distributions
Demonstrated transfer across different circuit topologies and technologies
limitations: Analysis limited to abstract; specific circuit domains and transfer performance metrics not detailed.
primary_theme: transferable parasitic estimation via graph contrastive learning
